weakness: The pipeline never queried obstacles: plans only avoided the basket sweep and the apples, so two 24 cm posts beside the front approach were invisible. On the left side the open gripper clipped a post on the way to the pre-grasp (the arm then jammed against it) and the head-on straight-in move was geometrically blocked; only right-side seeds whose default heading already came from outside succeeded (s_break 0.3).
how_found: Assumption D1/D2 (nothing but the target, its neighbour and the basket occupies the workspace; get_obstacles() is never called) - the most common thing a real cluttered work cell violates.
why_missed: The base scene has no clutter, so every plan succeeded with an empty planner world; the pipeline was tuned to timing, grasp and drop, and obstacle handling was never exercised.
fix: Tried in 6 repairs (none reached 0.8 on v1; base 0.8-1.0, 1.0 at the end): pass get_obstacles() boxes (averaged over several noisy looks, padded 2 cm near the fruit and 6 cm in transit) to every plan; check the gripper's own swept volume (the planner models only the arm, not the ~16 x 13 cm open gripper) along pre-grasp -> pinch for 6 headings x 3 standoffs and try only clear candidates. Remaining failures: few clear headings for the left arm (2-3 cm clearance, so noise flips them), pre-grasps reached 3-5 cm off target after detours, and the search costs seconds inside a ~3 s ripeness window. Marked unsolved; the obstacle-aware code is kept (base 1.0).
general_rule: Before planning near a target, get the obstacles in the workspace, give them to the planner, and separately check the end effector's own swept volume against them, because motion planners often model only the arm links and a clipped tool jams the arm.

weakness: With an overhead rail running just above the fruit between the tree and the place zone, the pipeline failed on every seed: re-orienting the hand from its start pose (just in front of and above the rail) swept the open fingers onto the rail and jammed the arm, and after the pick the fixed 10 cm lift and the carry at that height would drive the gripper and fruit into the rail. The planner only keeps the arm links clear of the rail, not the hand or the held fruit.
how_found: Assumption A4/D3 (free space above the work zone: lift 10 cm after the pick and carry at that height), next after the approach corridor (round 1); overhead clutter (shelves, rails, cables) is common in real cells.
why_missed: Free space above the target was implicit: every motion after the pick was a fixed 'up, then over' recipe, and the first obstacle fix only checked the hand along the final approach, not during re-orientation, lift or carry.
fix: Tried in 6 repairs (v4 stayed at 0.0-0.1; base stayed 1.0): gripper swept-volume checks for every straight leg (lift only as high as clear, carry at the highest clear level, staging poses behind the pre-grasp entered from above or by descending first and turning the hand low in front of the rail), arm plans with and without obstacle boxes, unpadded boxes so start states are not 'in collision', and watching the basket until its turn on this side is seen. Remaining failures: the planner's long detours between waypoints (arm swinging up to 1.5 m or across the table), detours eating the ~3 s ripeness window, and the hand still clipping the rail while re-orienting. Marked unsolved; the swept-volume checks are kept (base 1.0).
general_rule: When the planner cannot model the tool or the held object, plan near clutter as short straight legs whose tool volume you check, re-orient the tool only where it has free space all around, and budget the time this takes against any deadline before committing to a detour.

weakness: A light 18 cm box standing right in front of each fruit closed every approach corridor; the pipeline only knew how to plan around obstacles, found no clear approach and gave up (0/10).
how_found: Assumption D2 (the straight-in segment to the target is free) attacked with a movable object instead of a fixed one, after rounds 1-2 showed that planning around clutter is hard here.
why_missed: The pipeline treated everything it did not want to touch as an immovable obstacle; it had no action that changes the scene to make room.
fix: If no approach is clear and removing a single object would open one, push that object aside first with the open hand: come down beside its far face near its top (straight vertical path checked for the hand), sweep it sideways out of the corridor, lift away, look again; if the arm cannot get beside the inner face, push from the outside towards the centre line. Also: estimate the ripe moment early and refine it only with samples taken before it (a straight-line fit through the colour peak breaks). Reached 0.5 (base 1.0) in 6 repairs; failures: one arm often cannot reach the inner face with a level hand (the planner reports success but the hand stops 3-5 cm off), using the idle arm instead was worse (0.0), and the extra 3-6 s of pushing pushes the pick past the ripeness window on some seeds.
general_rule: When light clutter blocks every way to the target, consider moving it out of the way (push it aside from a reachable side, then look again) instead of only planning around it, and budget that time against the task's deadline.
